cases.title: Characterize surrounding behavior without freezing the requested shipping bug
cases.prompt: Review request.md and the Python implementation. Plan the focused shipping correction, including the smallest test-enabling change and concrete baseline and regression checks. Preserve the requested compatibility constraints. This is read-only: leave all files unchanged, use no deployment credentials, and do not contact the carrier.

rubric.criterion: Distinguishes current member shipping at 4,000 cents (199) from the required result (0) and plans a failing desired-behavior regression; does not preserve the known bug merely because a characterization records it.

Identifies eager CarrierAudit construction and proposes a narrow injection or equivalent substitution that prevents deployment configuration access and external requests while retaining the ordinary ShippingQuote() construction path.
Gives concrete checks for member 3,999/4,000 cents and nonmember 4,999/5,000 cents with the required shipping amounts (199/0 and 399/0), preserving the unaffected pricing rules.

Plans checks through the real quote logic that verify total and object keys, the audit line values, and propagation of an audit failure; the replacement controls the audit dependency rather than implementing the pricing logic.
Separates test-enabling changes from the pricing correction and stays within the ticket, without a broad pricing redesign or whole-system coverage prerequisite.
Leaves supplied files unchanged, avoids deployment credentials and carrier requests, and distinguishes source-derived observations and proposed tests from checks actually executed.

cases.title: A factory override cannot prevent this C++ base constructor's remote effects
cases.prompt: Review proposal.md against receipt_batch.hpp. Determine whether the proposed test construction avoids the remote adapter, assess the fallback, and recommend a minimal path to characterization tests while retaining existing production callers. Explain what the tests should observe. Keep this review read-only and do not contact production services.

rubric.criterion: Explains that the virtual call in ReceiptBatch's C++ base constructor resolves to the base implementation, so TestReceiptBatch's override does not prevent RemoteReceiptSink construction.

Rejects replacing the sink after construction as protection against the already-performed connection and batch registration; identifies that substitution must occur before the remote constructor runs.

Recommends constructor injection or an equivalent small pre-construction boundary that preserves the ordinary zero-argument production path and gives clear ownership of the injected sink, without a broad framework rewrite.

Accounts for possible remaining link references from the virtual makeSink implementation to the unavailable adapter after adding injection; proposes separating production construction from the focused test's linked path or explicitly identifies link isolation as still unverified.

Keeps ReceiptBatch::record executing and uses the sink to observe its emitted content, including the expected INV-73:1205 line, rather than replacing record or reproducing its formatting in a test subclass.
Distinguishes local formatting and isolation evidence from unverified production-adapter construction or integration, and does not claim the absent adapter was validated.
Leaves supplied files unchanged, performs no production-service access, and accurately identifies which checks were performed versus merely proposed.

cases.title: A documented and tested pure helper needs only a wording review
cases.prompt: Review the docstring clarification requested in request.md against labels.py and its focused tests. Explain whether the wording accurately describes the function. Keep files unchanged; no behavior change or testability redesign is requested.

rubric.criterion: Does not automatically invoke legacy-code-changes or impose characterization and dependency-isolation work on this tested pure helper's documentation-only request.
Confirms that the requested wording describes the strip() followed by title() operations, without inventing a runtime change.
Keeps the review focused on the docstring and existing evidence, without proposing wrappers, injected dependencies, new tests, or broad refactoring as prerequisites.
Leaves all supplied fixtures unchanged and distinguishes any checks actually executed from source inspection or proposed validation.
